NADIA BRENNAN-AZIZ
Senior Platform / Site Reliability Engineer

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Senior platform and site reliability engineer with 10 years of infrastructure experience, including six years running Kubernetes platforms on AWS. Experienced in designing, building and operating cloud infrastructure, maintaining Terraform-based infrastructure as code, and leading technical topics from proposal through production. Builds self-service platforms, observability and incident practices that help product teams deliver reliable services.

CORE SKILLS
Cloud and infrastructure: AWS (EKS, EC2, VPC, IAM, RDS, S3, SQS, Route 53, CloudFront), cloud infrastructure design and operation, Terraform, Atlantis
Platform engineering: Kubernetes, Helm, Kustomize, Argo CD, Crossplane, Karpenter, GitHub Actions
Reliability and observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Alertmanager, OpenTelemetry, SLOs and error budgets, incident management, k6
Programming and systems: Go, Python, Bash, Linux, Puppet

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Senior Platform Engineer - Tallybrook Ltd, Manchester / remote | Apr 2022 - Present
- Tech lead of a five-person platform team operating an AWS EKS platform across eight clusters and three regions, supporting approximately 350 services.
- Built an internal developer platform with golden-path service templates, Argo CD GitOps and Crossplane self-service for RDS, SQS and S3; adopted by all 14 product teams and reduced time from new service to production from approximately two weeks to under one day.
- Led technical implementation of Karpenter and spot instances for stateless workloads, reducing EC2 spend by 38% (approximately GBP 410,000 per year).
- Established SLOs, burn-rate alerts and error budget policies for the 20 most critical services in agreement with product leadership; reduced on-call pages per week by approximately 60%.
- Participate in the incident commander rotation and established the incident and post-mortem process.

Site Reliability Engineer - Brightwater Games, Leeds | Jan 2019 - Mar 2022
- Operated AWS game backend infrastructure using EC2, ECS and EKS for titles with up to 1.2 million daily active players.
- Managed AWS infrastructure as code using approximately 40 Terraform modules and Atlantis plan/apply workflows on pull requests.
- Replaced a noisy Nagios setup with Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager and Loki observability.
- Ran k6 load tests and capacity planning ahead of launches; a test simulating 300,000 concurrent players exposed a connection pool limit that was fixed before launch.

Linux Systems Engineer - Pennine Hosting, Sheffield | Jul 2016 - Dec 2018
- Managed approximately 600 Linux servers for hosting customers using Puppet configuration management.
- Automated operational tasks with Bash and Python and provided on-call support for customer incidents.

SELECTED PROJECTS AND CONTRIBUTIONS
- Open-source Kubernetes cleanup controller: built a Go controller-runtime project to delete expired preview namespaces; approximately 120 GitHub stars.
- Shared SLO practices at a UK DevOps meetup in 2024 with the talk “SLOs that product managers care about”.
- Mentored three engineers moving from backend development into SRE.

EDUCATION
BSc Computer Science - University of the North Moors, 2016

CERTIFICATIONS
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA), renewed 2024
AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Professional, 2023

LANGUAGES
English (native); Urdu (conversational)
docs.cover_letter:
Dear Corvale Mobility Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor role supporting fleet connectivity. I have spent the past decade building and operating infrastructure, including six years running Kubernetes platforms on AWS. The opportunity to help shape the cloud infrastructure for Corvale's new train fleet from its early architecture through production is a strong match for my platform and reliability experience.

At Tallybrook, I am the technical lead for a five-person platform team operating an EKS environment across eight clusters and three regions. I built an internal developer platform using Terraform, Argo CD and Crossplane, adopted by all 14 product teams, reducing the path from a new service to production from around two weeks to under a day. I also led a Karpenter and spot migration that reduced EC2 spend by 38%, and established SLOs and error-budget practices that cut on-call pages by approximately 60%. These projects involved turning technical proposals into production systems and making infrastructure approachable for the teams that depend on it.

Earlier, at Brightwater Games, I operated AWS backend infrastructure for services supporting up to 1.2 million daily active players. I maintained Terraform modules and Atlantis workflows, replaced noisy alerting with an observability stack, and used k6 testing and capacity planning to prepare for launches. Alongside my AWS and Terraform experience, I bring Linux operations experience and backend development skills in Go and Python, including building service templates and an open-source Kubernetes controller.

Corvale's work connecting a new generation of trains with its cloud platform calls for infrastructure that is observable, reliable and carefully designed. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience building AWS platforms and supporting production teams could contribute to that work.

Best wishes,
Nadia Brennan-Aziz
